name: Pull-up bar

image.credit: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Gymnastics rings hung from a doorway pull-up bar 02.jpg
image.caption: Pull-up bar

lead: A pull-up bar is a fixed horizontal bar, mounted in a doorway, on a wall, on a ceiling or on a freestanding frame, from which the user hangs to perform pull-ups, chin-ups and hanging core work. It is among the cheapest pieces of equipment that trains the whole back.

In looksmaxxing it is associated with the V-taper: wider lats and a stronger upper back make the shoulders look broader relative to the waist, and strong scapular muscles support a more upright posture. Progress is tracked by repetitions, added weight or harder variations.

paras: Vertical pulling against bodyweight loads the latissimus dorsi, biceps, lower trapezius and rear shoulder muscles. Electromyography studies of pull-up variations show high lat activity in all common grips with only modest differences between them, so the exercise mainly works through progressive overload (more reps, added load, slower tempo) rather than through any special grip.

Doorway bars can mar trim or fail if installed poorly, and wall-mounted bars need studs or masonry. Overuse injuries of the elbow and shoulder are the common problems, particularly with kipping or high weekly volume. Many beginners cannot yet do a pull-up and need bands or negatives first. The claim that pull-ups build back width is supported by general resistance-training evidence; the specific superiority of wide-grip variants is not well established.
